$comment: REBUTTAL_CARD.json example + required conventions (EMNLP/ARR). One card per campaign; instantiate.py renders CLAUDE/GOAL/SPEC/VERIFY/RESOURCE from it; when a card is missing, r0a extracts the card from papers/<slug>. paper-agnostic: changing case = changing the card, without modifying the harness. ★Required/conventions: reviewers[].id, reviewers[].initial_overall (EMNLP overall assessment, integer /5 —— both the zone bar and verify use it; the old ICLR initial_rating(/10) is deprecated and read only for compatibility with legacy cards), target.require_raise_on(P0, offense), target.maintain(OA>=4, defense), n_strategies (must equal the number of enabled entries in strategies/MANIFEST.json), allow_new_experiments (when false, the driver must hard-skip r4), max_iter.
title: Learning to Rebut: A First-Principles Argument Compiler
word_limit: one comment box per reviewer (~300–600 words)
paper_claims: C1: We propose mechanism M, which resolves the conflict between A and B; this is the core contribution
C2: On benchmark X, it improves by 13.6 points over the strongest baseline
C3: The theoretical analysis provides a convergence guarantee for M (Thm 1)
concern_seeds: R2: The method is merely a combination of A+B, with limited novelty
R1: A comparison with SOTA method Z is missing
R1: The ablation study is insufficient, so it is unclear whether M is actually useful
R3: The presentation could be clearer; §3.2 is difficult to read
